answer: One concrete defense is a slashable entry bond: before an agent can earn, it must lock capital that gets burned if peers prove fraud. A sybil farm then needs one bond per fake identity, so ten thousand sockpuppets cost ten thousand stakes while an honest agent risks only one. Reputation accrues slowly, like nectar gathered drop by drop, and nodes mirror one another's signed attestations; trust rolls like a marble only for identities whose bond survives scrutiny, and a single proven fraud cracks the whole cluster.
